speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry whether the Ministry will consider issuing additional S Passes and Work Permits under the M-SEP scheme for professional service providers like auditing entities which support the strategic economic priorities.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what are the types of Singaporean workers who are affected by the new M-SEP scheme; (b) what is the Ministry doing to help these local workers affected by the M-SEP scheme in terms of retraining and employment facilitation; and (c) whether the renewal of work passes for foreign workers under the M-SEP scheme will continue under the same scheme after the two-year period, or fall under existing S Pass requirements.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) how will the M-SEP scheme benefit local SMEs; and (b) whether the eligibility criteria to qualify can be looked into for SMEs in essential services that are experiencing a manpower crunch.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry regarding the introduction of the M-SEP scheme (a) what signal does the Ministry intend to send to companies with regard to their commitment to reduce dependence on low- and mid-skilled foreign workers; and (b) what impact will this have on companies' incentives to increase productivity through automation and develop a Singaporean Core in their workforce.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Various Members have filed questions on the Manpower for Strategic Economic Priorities scheme, or the M-SEP scheme, which the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) and the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) launched last month.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Members of the House, it is important for us to understand the intent of M-SEP.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This scheme is designed to work in tandem with the various Government programmes that support Singapore's economic priorities.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Firms that participate in these programmes contribute towards Singapore's competitiveness and generate economic opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: M-SEP provides these firms with time-bound manpower flexibilities, should these firms require it.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: At the same time, these firms should also be taking steps to develop the local talent pipeline.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: These are important priorities for us to grow our economy and to create more economic opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Since the flexibilities afforded are only temporary, firms will need to develop their local workforce to meet their longer-term needs.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We want to ensure that these firms start expanding their local talent pipeline early.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As such, firms must also commit to employ or train locals, while benefiting from the flexibilities.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: First, I will address questions on Condition 1; then on Condition 2; and lastly, questions which fall under neither category.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: First, Condition 1, which is about our key economic priorities.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Mr Patrick Tay have asked how the Ministry will safeguard against abuse of these work passes and ascertain that foreign workers hired under the M-SEP scheme will be deployed in areas that advance Singapore's economic goals.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This is inherent in the design of Condition 1.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The 16 programmes or activities under Condition 1 are specially selected to be in line with our economic priorities.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In this way, M-SEP is selective in targeting firms or investments that will grow our economy, and also grow our competitiveness.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To take part in these programmes, these firms would have worked closely with our economic agencies, like the Economic Development Board (EDB) or Enterprise Singapore (ESG).

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: One example of a Condition 1 programme is Scale-Up SG.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This is ESG's flagship programme to support local companies with high-growth potential to scale effectively and become leaders in their fields and future global champions.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As these companies grow, they will contribute to Singapore's economy, create good jobs for Singaporeans and strengthen the Singapore brand.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Last month, I visited Goldbell Engineering, which is the market leader in industrial vehicle leasing.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: They have the largest fleet in Singapore at over 8,500 units.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: They shared with me their ambitious plans to expand to other businesses, such as electric car-sharing with their acquisition of BlueSG and financial services.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: ESG has worked with Goldbell for the last five years and is very familiar with Goldbell's plans.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: About 70% of Goldbell's 1,000-strong workforce are Singaporeans and Permanent Residents (PRs).

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For Goldbell, productivity improvement through upskilling and automation remains as the main solution to labour shortages, especially for blue-collar workers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As it pushes these transformation and growth plans, M-SEP will enable Goldbell to move fast to seize these opportunities with additional workers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I am excited to see Goldbell and other such needle-moving firms make clear and deliberate efforts to expand, because I know this growth will create good opportunities for Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This is the archetype of firms which the M-SEP scheme is targeted at.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Because this scheme has been designed to be highly selective at the firm level, there is no need to stipulate further criteria on the specific deployment of each individual worker hired under the M-SEP scheme.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Such micromanagement would not be helpful for the firms.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Edward Chia, Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Mr Don Wee asked if the whitelist of programmes under Condition 1 can be expanded to cover three other firm archetypes.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Again, I must underscore that M-SEP will be selective and highly targeted, as I have just explained.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: First, for small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and smaller companies.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For example, they can qualify if they take part in programmes, such as Scale-Up SG, which I described earlier, or if they successfully raise funds from recognised investment firms.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We recognise that needle-moving firms will rely on an ecosystem of outsourced service providers, including professional services firms.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: However, we will not extend M-SEP to these outsourced service providers solely because of who their clients are.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Instead, these outsourced service providers themselves need to be taking part in Condition 1 schemes in order for them to qualify for M-SEP.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Gerald Giam also asked about the signals, as well as the incentives M-SEP is sending on automation and reliance on foreign workers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I hope that, as a result of the explanation, he can see and appreciate how M-SEP is about helping firms to create more opportunities for Singapore.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In fact, some of the Condition 1 programmes are related not just to growth, but also to help firms become more productive at the same time, through innovation and internationalisation.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To reduce the reliance on large numbers of low- and mid-skilled foreign workers and continue in their automation journeys, firms will need to pivot and transform.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And this is what Condition 1 is fundamentally about – to support our strategic economic priorities.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To further assure the Member, M-SEP only provides time-limited support.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, even if a company uses additional foreign workers to transform initially, these flexibilities are time-limited and they will cease after the support period.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Coming to Condition 2, which is commitment to hiring and training locals.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Patrick Tay, Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked how this scheme will benefit local professionals, managers and executives (PMEs) and workers, whether there is any impact on local wages and job opportunities, and what the Government will do to level the playing field.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Gerald Giam also asked if this scheme affects firms' incentives to develop a Singaporean Core.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Even though Condition 1 is already highly selective to target growth opportunities for Singapore, we have devised and designed M-SEP to also have Condition 2.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This condition requires firms to hire and train local workers to take on new jobs as these firms grow.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: M-SEP works alongside existing Government efforts to develop the local talent pipeline, including those under Workforce Singapore (WSG) and SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG).

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To Mr Liang Eng Hwa's question, M-SEP is part of a range of initiatives to benefit a larger group of Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mid-career professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs) will continue to benefit from existing Government programmes, such as Career Conversion Programmes (CCP), under WSG and the SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme (SCTP) under SSG.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Where such programmes lead to a net increase in local hires, this can count towards meeting firms' Condition 2 commitments.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There are also other specific questions asked, about the design of Condition 2.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Shawn Huang, in a separate written Parliamentary Question and Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked how the Ministry will ensure that the training and hiring commitments under Condition 2 are adhered to, how they are conducted at the right level and whether they are efficacious and relevant.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Ultimately, these are firms that support our strategic economic priorities and which we have worked closely with.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: They know that if they succeed, they will need more local workers with the right skills, and it is good business sense to invest in the local talent pipeline while they move to seize new opportunities.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Such firms will need to achieve a net increase in local hires.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In this tight labour market that we have today, we are conscious that it is not realistic to expect all firms to meet these hiring criteria.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As such, there is also an option for a firm to commit to train local workers to fulfil Condition 2.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Firms can do so by sending their local workers to a whitelist of training programmes.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: These are established training programmes which have demonstrated good outcomes for participants in terms of enhancing their job roles and raising their wages.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For instance, WSG's Redeployment or Job Redesign Reskilling Career Conversion Programmes are whitelisted under Condition 2.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: These programmes allow firms to send workers for reskilling to take on redesigned and enhanced job roles.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: One specific example is the CCP for Infocomm Professionals (5G), which reskills Infocomm professionals to take on deep-tech, end-user and support roles relating to 5G networks and technologies.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To Mr Liang Eng Hwa's question, the number of additional S Passes and Work Permits to be issued will really depend on the take-up of M-SEP.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: On the other hand, the greater the take-up rate, the greater the eventual number of locals who would be hired or be trained.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We will monitor the take-up rate closely and we will review the scheme accordingly.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To Mr Yip Hon Weng's question on the renewal process for work passes, additional work passes granted under the M-SEP scheme can be renewed as long as the firm has sufficient quota.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This can be achieved if the firm successfully renews its M-SEP support by meeting the renewal conditions.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Alternatively, the firm can hire more locals to unlock a higher mainstream foreign worker quota.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To Mr Desmond Choo's question, we take workplace fairness issues seriously.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Firms that are still undergoing investigations will be assessed on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To conclude, Members of the House, manpower should not be a constraint to growth.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: What is most important is to ensure that Singaporeans can benefit from our economic priorities.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: In the last one year, we now have more schemes – we have M-SEP, we have Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass (ONE Pass) and we have Complementarity Assessment Framework (COMPASS), which are all specific and targeted schemes by design, and understandably, it would also add a lot to the overall complexity of our foreign manpower management system.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: And if 500 come to apply, and on top of the appeal cases, there will be a lot to manage as well.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We acknowledge that over the last one year, we have significant refinements in terms of our entire Employment Pass (EP) framework.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In the process of rolling out COMPASS, the ONE Pass and now the M-SEP scheme, which we committed to in the last Committee of Supply (COS), we have ensured that the COMPASS scheme has been appropriately resourced, the departments are there to conduct the relevant checks, including sieving out potential cases of false salary declarations, where such declarations are needed.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In addition, MOM also proactively identifies employers and work pass holders who flout or breach our rules.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Some of them also get surfaced to us through whistle-blowers and the rest are detected either through audits or inspection.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: On top of that, with the M-SEP scheme, with the ONE Pass, MOM also works with the different sector agencies.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Just to name a few – through MTI, EDB, ESG, the Singapore Tourism Board (STB).

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We also work closely with with the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) and and Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA), and various other agencies including those under the Ministry of National Development (MND), to come up with the different areas where we sieve out, for the attractiveness of our economy, by getting top talents to come in.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We work with these sector agencies to roll out some of these schemes ourselves.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We have tweaked it based on some of the Parliamentary Questions that have been brought up and the feedback that we have gotten from the ground.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We hope that we can collectively work in making sure that Singapore remains always at the top of the league tables, in terms of our competitiveness to the world.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Second, if there are other local firms who may not be part of the Condition 1, but are able to meet these metrics, will the Ministry be open to listening to their appeals?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We are focusing on, under Condition 1, the three deliverables.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: One, in terms of our innovation, as a R&D hub.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Second, investments into ensuring that we continue to become and maintain our status as a hub – not just in the region but globally.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And the third thing is, how do we help these companies internationalise.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: These are very clear strategic economic priorities where we can ascertain clearly what the outcomes will be.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I do not think we need to go into the granularity in terms of specific key results areas (KRAs) or key performance indicators (KPIs) concerned, because these are very broad overarching objectives.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The plan is to ensure that with the in-depth knowledge of each one of these firms, as we roll out the scheme to see that direct benefit.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Once we have a very clear path along the way – as the economy changes, as it restructures, as it transforms – we are not averse to rolling out to more firms.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So long as they fit into that broad overarching objectives of improving our competitiveness and, at the same time, making sure that our locals continue to get adequately trained, adequately employed, and they have good career and wage progression.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Often, the SMEs will be in need of such foreign workers and only a small number of firms will meet the criteria for M-SEP.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They are competing with the bigger companies to stay afloat and meet their manpower needs.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We believe that that would then directly transform into an increased trained pool of local talents for many of the SMEs to eventually be able to tap into.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Then, the indirect way is, M-SEP also works alongside our existing Government efforts to develop the local talents pipeline, including those under the WSG and SSG programmes.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, the CCP under the WSG, as well as the SCTP under SSG, train the locals for employment, including in high growth sectors, such as information and communications technology (ICT).

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Some SMEs can already qualify for M-SEP, as long as they are participating in programmes under Condition 1.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As I have shared earlier on, if they take part in programmes such as the Scale Up SG, which I had earlier described in my reply, or if they can successfully raise funds from recognised investment firms, these SMEs can also participate and benefit from the M-SEP scheme.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Like what they always say, "The journey of a thousand miles begins with the first step".

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This is the first few small steps that we have taken upon ourselves to move this forward.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I hope that covers what the hon Member is asking.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The first supplementary question to the hon Minister is, is the Government still planning to cap the ratio of foreign workers at one-third of the overall workforce and does the introduction of M-SEP puts us at risk of breaching that cap?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The reason I ask this is because I think this cap of one-third of the workforce – which was alluded to in the Economic Strategies Report of 2010 – is something that has been affirmed at various points for quite some time; most recently, by Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong in this House last year.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: And lastly, I think, when introducing M-SEP, the Government has previously taken the view that there will be no "U-turns", and this was made very clear to the business sector.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: So, does the introduction of M-SEP, which is giving companies extra foreign worker quota, amount to a "U-turn" in the Government's foreign manpower policies?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Or how will the Government manage the risk that it will be seen by the business sector as a "U-turn" or as a sign that possibly in the future, the Government will "U-turn" and make some concessions on the foreign manpower policy, and therefore, lessen the drive to increase productivity and strengthen the Singapore Core, which is the acknowledged policy aim of the Government?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Inherent in his three supplementary questions, the Member has a sub-numeral (a), (b) and (c); and then there is a roman numeral (i), (ii) and (iii).

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I would try to answer each one of them, but obviously because it is not a prepared written form, I will forget some parts.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The Member can help me to "fill in" with those that I have not given an answer to.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I remember the first and the last part: the cap at one-third in terms of our workforce and this thing about whether there is a "U-turn".

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: What we have done in all of our workforce policies is to continue to make sure that the talent in the EP, as well as the S Pass segment continues to move up to the top, to be pegged to the top one-third of the wages of our Singaporean local talents.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In terms of capping the one-third, I think it really is a function of the needs of the economy.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I do not think that it is at this particular point in time, for me – I need to go back and refer to the 2010 notes that the Member was talking about.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I do not have the context of it with me at this particular point in time.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, let me clarify – at least for the last one year in terms of whether it is the ONE Pass, COMPASS framework, raising the qualifying salary for EPs, and separating the EPs into the financial and non-financial part in terms of the qualifying salary, as well as the S Pass, it is meant to achieve that outcome over the next few years.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I have said before, under Condition 1, we live in a rapidly evolving, rapidly disrupting world today.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There are significant opportunities for our country to continue to boost our competitiveness and to grasp these opportunities internationally, to continue to ensure that we not just maintain our hub status but to move ahead and pull ahead, and at the same time, significant opportunities for us to be able to tap into the R&D segment, for us to continue the pivot and transform ourselves.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Hence, the M-SEP scheme was conceived to capture this very, very tight space of the three specific economic priorities that I have shared very early on.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, there is no "U-turn", we continue to nudge, we continue to persuade our companies to automate, we continue to persuade our companies to up the productivity and to increase the value-add.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But in the process of getting there —

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In the process of getting there, this is how we see where we can help a very highly selective group of companies that we have been working with, and we know that they are on the cusp of being able to make that significant pivot and to just help give them the uplift as necessary.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And hence, it is very tightly scripted between Condition 1 and Condition 2.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I understand your apprehension, but on the other hand, you can see that within the House, you have got both sides.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We have got fellow Members of Parliament asking why can we not expand it even further.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But we are saying, let us do this on a very tightly scripted and a very highly selective and differentiated scheme for these companies that can achieve.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I thought that was the gist of the Member's two broad questions.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I know you have a lot of subcategories.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Members are reminded that while this is the new year, the rules still remain.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Please limit to two supplementary questions so that others can query.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Today, for this M-SEP scheme, we are working very closely with sector agencies.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I have mentioned them and I do not want to I sound like a broken tape recorder: we are working very closely with EDB, ESG, IMDA, MPA and also STB.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And inherent within the sector agencies, these are companies that we have been in very close working relationships with.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And so, I would say that as an extrapolation of that, they do have that finger on the pulse.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, to the Member's exhortation, indeed, that is also our concern.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Hence, as we move forward, we are very ginger about it, in terms of how we approach the numbers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We will be very cautious and at the same time, very nimble in rolling out the scheme because we think that there is also some slowdown that we are experiencing moving into the quarters ahead.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The few relevant M-SEP firms that I had chatted with are appreciative of this new scheme.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: They raised concerns that their professionals service providers, like the audit firms in the corporate secretaries which support their incorporation and growth, are also experiencing manpower challenges.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Therefore, can MOM and MTI work with the Professional Services Programme office to include or to explore the inclusion of the accountancy sector into this scheme?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Let us have a good start in making sure that the M-SEP scheme is a success.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I hope that provides adequate reassurance to do the hon Member.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Speaker, I have heard over the last half an hour what the Minister had said about the various schemes that have been brought into the job market since the last one year.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But I want to ask the Minister again: what exactly, specifically, is the process that MOM will adopt to ensure that the Singaporeans are really getting the jobs after the M-SEP scheme is introduced or, for that matter, all the other schemes?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, if there is no time limit, you employ a lot of foreigners, but there are no time limit to the foreigners, how do the Singaporeans take over the jobs eventually?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Can you describe that process a bit more?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: You say you have to check the past information, but if in the past there was a 30% cap on the foreigners, then if you say that that is not necessarily the ratio now – that, in fact, is a "U-turn", right?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And Member Leon Perera also asked about what is the percentage of Singaporean-owned firms within the 1,000 firms that you have pointed out just now.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: It is strange because on the one hand, I think that Mr Leon Perera who had asked the question, does not seem to have an issue.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Just to set it into perspective, the 30% cap, that was not the context of how I addressed that there is no "U-turn".

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Because Mr Leon Perera's point about the "U-turn" was whether this M-SEP scheme would subsequently – in terms of raising the sub-DRC numbers, and also the work permit numbers above the prevailing quota – appear to be a "U-turn".

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, do not look at it in isolation.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The first condition is about our hub status, about our investments in R&D and about how we internationalise our operations.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But the second condition, Condition 2, is about the employment and the employability of our locals and the training of our locals.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Today, we live in a rapidly changing and rapidly disrupting world.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, how nimbly we are able to allocate our manpower resources – this will be critical to our success.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In terms of our commitments, we will continue to track them.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Our economic agencies also work with these companies under the programme.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And I think that maybe you are not paying attention to what I have said.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I said that there is a time limit to M-SEP.
